**Work items are for agents. Todos are for humans.** They share a word in ordinary
speech and nothing else, and conflating them is how a work plan comes to hold
two kinds of thing that need different handling.

A **work item** is process state an agent keeps while doing work: claimed before
starting so a sibling session avoids it, kept current as the work proceeds,
and closed with a record of what changed. The store is `beans/`, committed,
so it survives a reclaimed container and is visible to every other session.

A **todo** is a person's own reminder — what they mean to look at next. It is
theirs to create, reorder and discard on no schedule but their own, and
nothing about an agent's process should be deciding when it is done.

This page describes the first in full. The second is **not built yet** and
says so.

## Two things that share a word
{: #two-things-one-word data-fa-label="sec:beans-and-todos-two-things-one-word" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/edit/main/docs/source/guides-beans-and-todos/two-things-one-word.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/guides-beans-and-todos/two-things-one-word.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/guides-beans-and-todos/two-things-one-word.md" data-repo="litlfred/cat-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="two-things-one-word.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-beans-and-todos/two-things-one-word.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-beans-and-todos/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="two-things-one-word.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-beans-and-todos/two-things-one-word.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-beans-and-todos/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

The two have different owners, lifecycles and failure modes.

| | **Work item** | **Todo** |
|---|---|---|
| Owner | An agent session | A person |
| Purpose | Process state for work in flight | A reminder of intent |
| Store | `beans/`, committed and shared | Not yet defined |
| Created by | An agent, after an exact-title check | The person, whenever they like |
| Closed by | The agent that did the work, with a summary | The person, on their own judgement |
| Visible to | Every sibling session | The person, primarily |
| Failure mode | Duplicated, or closed by the wrong session | Forgotten |

**The failure modes are what make the split worth keeping.** A duplicated work item
starves the work plan of signal, and an unguarded re-run can duplicate most of
it. A forgotten todo
inconveniences one person. Machinery sized for the first is ceremony on the
second, and machinery sized for the second is nowhere near enough for the
first.

<div class="bpmn-figure" id="figure-the-agent-bean-lifecycle">
  <img src="{{ '/assets/img/workflows/bean-lifecycle.svg' | relative_url }}"
       alt="BPMN swimlane diagram with two lanes. In the agent's lane: durable work is identified, the agent runs an exact-title search before creating anything, then a gateway asks whether the bean already exists. If not, it creates one; if it does, a second gateway asks whose it is. A bean owned by someone else routes to the lower lane — sibling session or human — where the only action is to leave it alone and coordinate, ending there. The agent's own or an unclaimed bean is claimed as in-progress, worked on with the body kept current, and then reaches an outcome gateway with three branches: done goes to complete, not wanted goes to scrap with reasons and never delete, and blocked goes to recording the blocker and handing it back. All three converge on a single end event, state recorded.">
</div>

[Open the BPMN source](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant/blob/main/processes/bean-lifecycle.bpmn){: .btn .btn-outline }

The diagram above is the whole cycle. Three of its edges matter most.

**The first step is a search, not a creation.** `beans create` is not
idempotent: it mints a fresh identifier on every call and de-duplicates on
nothing, so re-entering a step duplicates the plan rather than doing nothing.
The exact-title check is what stands between a repeated workflow step and a
corpus of near-identical work items.

**Ownership is a gateway, not a courtesy.** A work item another session claimed is
not yours to resolve, scrap or delete. Claiming is how two sessions avoid
picking up the same item; closing someone else's is how one of them loses work
it had not finished reporting.

**"Blocked" is not "not wanted".** A blocked work item returns to `todo` with its
blocker recorded and something said about what would clear it. Leaving it
`in-progress` is worse than either: an item nobody is progressing reads, to
every other session, as active work.

## A bean is never deleted
{: #never-delete data-fa-label="sec:beans-and-todos-never-delete" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/edit/main/docs/source/guides-beans-and-todos/never-delete.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/guides-beans-and-todos/never-delete.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/guides-beans-and-todos/never-delete.md" data-repo="litlfred/cat-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="never-delete.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-beans-and-todos/never-delete.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-beans-and-todos/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="never-delete.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-beans-and-todos/never-delete.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-beans-and-todos/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

`beans delete` exists in the CLI. **Do not use it.**

Work that turns out not to be wanted is **scrapped** — `status: scrapped`,
with a section saying why. That is what "disable" means here; the CLI has no
disabled state, and its vocabulary is `draft`, `todo`, `in-progress`,
`completed`, `scrapped`.

A scrapped work item records that something was considered and rejected, and on
what grounds, which stops the next agent re-entering the same dead end. A deleted work item leaves a sibling session unable
to tell abandonment from accident, and leaves the next agent free to start
over on the thing you already ruled out.

The rule is stated here, and in the diagram's own documentation, because the
CLI offers the operation.

## Engine operations are not CLI calls
{: #two-layers data-fa-label="sec:beans-and-todos-two-layers" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/edit/main/docs/source/guides-beans-and-todos/two-layers.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/guides-beans-and-todos/two-layers.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/guides-beans-and-todos/two-layers.md" data-repo="litlfred/cat-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="two-layers.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-beans-and-todos/two-layers.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-beans-and-todos/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="two-layers.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-beans-and-todos/two-layers.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-beans-and-todos/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

Two different things can change a work item, and a step that confuses them will
announce an effect it does not have.

**The workflow engine** performs `claim`, `note` and `resolve` on a process
instance's own work item when a step marked `<cat-harness.processes:bean op="…"/>` completes.
`claim` sets `in-progress` and is idempotent; `note` appends; `resolve`
completes the work item **only once the instance itself has completed**, because
whether work is done is a judgement and a work item is not closed on someone else's
say-so.

**The agent** does everything else with the `beans` CLI: creating, scrapping,
retitling, setting a blocker. The engine has no operation for any of these.

**When you add a bean-marked step,** use one of the three operations the
engine implements, and say in the step's documentation which parts are the
agent's own CLI calls. `bun run cat check:workflow-refs` will catch a skill
reference that does not resolve; it cannot catch a plausible attribute the
engine never reads.

## Human todos — not built yet
{: #human-todos data-fa-label="sec:beans-and-todos-human-todos" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/edit/main/docs/source/guides-beans-and-todos/human-todos.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/guides-beans-and-todos/human-todos.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/guides-beans-and-todos/human-todos.md" data-repo="litlfred/cat-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="human-todos.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-beans-and-todos/human-todos.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-beans-and-todos/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="human-todos.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-beans-and-todos/human-todos.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-beans-and-todos/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

**Not built yet.**

A person's todos need a cycle of their own, and none of it exists:

- **When a todo is shown.** Surfacing every open item on every turn is noise;
  surfacing none is a list nobody reads. Whatever the rule is, it is not the
  same as the work-plan priming an agent gets at session start.
- **When a person may create one**, and through what — chat, a command, the
  session-start surface.
- **How one is retired.** A person abandoning a reminder is ordinary and needs
  no "reasons for scrapping" section; the work item rules do not transfer.

Until that is designed, **do not repurpose work items for it.** A store whose
entries are claimed by sessions, closed with change summaries and never
deleted is the wrong shape for a reminder somebody wants to drop without
ceremony — and mixing the two would put items in the agent work plan that no
agent should be acting on.

## What the work plan holds right now
{: #work-plan-state data-fa-label="sec:beans-and-todos-work-plan-state" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/edit/main/docs/source/guides-beans-and-todos/work-plan-state.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/guides-beans-and-todos/work-plan-state.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/guides-beans-and-todos/work-plan-state.md" data-repo="litlfred/cat-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="work-plan-state.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-beans-and-todos/work-plan-state.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-beans-and-todos/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="work-plan-state.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-beans-and-todos/work-plan-state.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-beans-and-todos/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

The rest of this page says what a work item **is**. This section says what the
store currently **holds** — read live from
[`/assets/beans/index.json`]({{ '/assets/beans/index.json' | relative_url }}), the projection
`gen-docs-pages.ts` writes from `beans/defs/` on every build, beside the todo
index it has published for longer. It exists because a work plan nobody can
look at is one nobody checks.

**What the dashboard shows.** The counts, as numbers, because they are a
headline. The work plan as a tree, goal → epic → feature → story, because the
question a reader brings is "where does this sit"; the type filter and the search prune that tree
to what matches and open it down to them. The store's `task` type is shown as
**story**, since a Task here is a BPMN task. The findings, as a list with an
icon and a label on every row, because a status colour never carries meaning
alone.

**The findings are computed from committed data only, and one of them is
missing on purpose.** A stale `in-progress` detector would have to read the
clock, and the projection is gated on exact content — anything computed
against the clock changes the file on every build and the staleness gate then
fires forever. So the projection publishes each work item's `updated_at` as a fact
and the page computes age when you open it. Age therefore moves without the
file moving, which is the right way round.

**There is a fuller view, and it is browsable.** Every declared state graph
gets its own visualiser at the path this layer already uses for that graph —
`/beans/`, `/todos/`, and one for each of the others. A rendered asset is
addressed by its layer's **name** with the **declared graph as a path
segment**; this layer elides its own name because its `docs/` is what the
site serves. The `harness-requirements` skill names that URL as the
obligation. There is no index above them,
because `/` is the documentation site's, so each page lists its siblings.

**A graph with no projection says so.** `qa`, `health`, `issue-marks` and
`uploads` are declared state graphs that nothing publishes a projection for
yet. Their dashboards say exactly that, rather than rendering zeros for a
store nobody read, because a dashboard that opens at zero cannot be told from
a store with nothing in it.

**Every identifier on those pages is a link.** A work item id resolves to the work item's
file, an issue or pull-request number to the forge, and each finding carries a
pencil to where writing actually happens. A reference that cannot be resolved
stays as plain text, which is the visible difference between *"follow this"*
and *"this points somewhere I could not reach"*.

**What is not here.** Where a work item sits in a BPMN process. That join needs `beans/workflows/`, the declared
`workflow-state` graph, and it is empty — so a position view would report
"nowhere" for every work item in the store. It waits for instance state to exist.
